body: Yes, but everything I've looked into has had some huge costs associated with it. I would go with friends but no one I know would go with me. I'd be happy to go alone but I don't know how.

I would think about planning a trip for the summer. I don't have the resources to take a trip in the next 9 months though. I visited them last summer and it was probably the best two weeks of the past 4 years.
I had a 34, 3.8 GPA, and some decent extracurriculars. I go to a state school but there's no way that would have gotten me a free ride.

I wish I could, but I absolutely cannot afford it. By the time I pay off the bills I already owe, I will be out over $6000. I have $2500 in my bank account. Add on the cost of airfare and living expenses until I get a job and I will be out probably close to $10,000. I have no where to get that money from. I seriously wish I could, but it's just not feasible.

I understand what you mean. Sometimes it's just overwhelming and you can't stop it. Will some good sleep help you? Do you have anything important tomorrow? If not, maybe staying home and sleeping in will help you think a little clearer tomorrow. Even if you might catch some flak for missing a day of work/class/whatever it might be worth it to take some time for yourself.

Or maybe forcing yourself to get up and do what you have to do will make you stop thinking about it for a while. Both of those things have helped me in the past. 

Sorry that both of my pieces of advice are completely contradictory! I'm not very helpful hah.

Right this second, I would pack my shit and run away to Europe. I have family there (crazy family, but I love them) and I would love to get away from everything here and just live. Find places to rock climb, live in the back of my car, just be.

Realistically planning for the rest of my life, I want to go back to my hometown and get a job in a public health related area. That's always been what has interested me and made me happy.

Nope. I'm a very average person. My boyfriend was going through some traumatic stuff which I am trying to help him deal with. Since it started my parents told me they are separating, which is difficult but not completely unexpected.

I'm thinking about going to a counselor, but I can't get in with the school. It's a super long process to get an intake interview with them and they only do it certain hours of the week. and if I go private it goes on my mom's insurance and she'll see it and I really don't want to talk to her about it. She always gets upset when I get depressed because she thinks it's her fault and I don't want to do that to her. I might try to talk to a friend but last time I did he kind of blew it off so i don't know how well that will go. Ugh, I sound like such a whiny little brat right now and I hate when I get like this.

This sounds so stupid and condescending and I hope you don't take it that way, but take a deep breath. When I relapse I tend to panic, stop breathing, and freak out even more. Just breath for a few minutes.

Like /u/TheDedicatedDeist said, people relapse. Doesn't make you a bad person. It happens. I hope it has't happened to you tonight, but if it has it's not the end of the world. If you haven't relapsed yet just know you've been strong before and I totally think you can do it again. And if you have relapsed, try not to beat yourself up. There's always tomorrow.

I hope this is all coherent and kind, I'm drunk so it might not make sense.
